transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Luis Martinez (Redwood CSM); Ethan Cole (Nebula PM); Sofia Nguyen (Nebula Eng Lead); Mark Anders (Nebula CTO, joined 00:08:30); Aisha Khan (Nebula Security)

Summary (auto): Agreeing on POC milestones, benchmark plan, dataset and access needs. Some minor transcription noise.

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick rol call, i'm jordan from redwood, with priya our se and luis. how's every- how's everyone doing?
00:08 Ethan Cole: good, thanks jordan, excited to get this kicked off. big thing for us is proving latency and cost at scale, also security bar.
00:20 Priya Rao: awesome, i'll walk through the proposed milestone timeline and the benchmark plan we usually run, and we'll align success criteria.
00:35 Sofia Nguyen: quick note, we run a mix of short queries (1-2 prompt turns) and longer summarizations up to ~1.2k tokens, so variability matters.
00:48 Jordan Lee: great, can you quantify expected qps or concurrent rps?
00:55 Ethan Cole: typical steady state 20 qps, peaks up to 120 qps for 30s bursts. average turn length about 600 tokens.
:01:10 Priya Rao: ok that helps. for the POC we recommend a staged benchmark: baseline (hosted small), dedicated trial for throughput, then a stability run. we'll measure latency p50/p95, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens.
01:30 Sofia Nguyen: do you have standard targets? like p95 under 300ms?
01:36 Priya Rao: we usually set p50 target 60-120ms and p95 under 400-450ms for small prompts on 8k context models; but for longer seqs numbers vary. we should capture target per workload.
01:58 Ethan Cole: our internal success criteria: p95 < 500ms for short prompts, end-to-end cost less than $0.03 per 1k tokens, and quality delta < 3% regression on our eval prompts.
02:15 Jordan Lee: great to capture that. i'll put those in the success criteria doc.
02:28 Luis Martinez: for timeline, propose kickoff today, infra/access/setup in week 1, baseline benchmarks week 2, midpoint review week 4, exec readout week 7.
02:45 Ethan Cole: that sounds reasonable. can we lock the dates?
03:00 Priya Rao: proposed: kickoff 2026-03-03, access & infra 2026-03-04 to 03-10, baseline benchmarks 03-11 to 03-17, dedicated throughput test 03-18 to 03-24, midpoint review 03-31, stability run 04-01 to 04-07, exec readout 04-21.
03:28 Sofia Nguyen: we may need a little longer for data prep, can we push baseline a week?
03:36 Jordan Lee: flexible — what if nebula targets to have the sample dataset in by 03-09, that keeps schedule intact.
03:46 Ethan Cole: we can do 03-09 for sample data.
03:50 Priya Rao: good. i'll also need network access details — vpc peering vs transit gateway? what infra are you on?
04:02 Sofia Nguyen: we run AWS in us-west-2, vpc peering preferred, but we have strict firewall rules.
04:12 Aisha Khan: from security: we need SOC2 attestation, SAML SSO, audit logs, and keys to be managed in our KMS. can you provide an SOC2 report and KMS integration doc?
04:29 Jordan Lee: yes we can provide SOC2 and we support customer-managed keys via KMS for private deployments. for hosted we have encryption at rest but we can discuss VPC/private options for data in transit.
04:42 Aisha Khan: also need log retention policies and RBAC details.
04:48 Luis Martinez: noted, we'll share our security pack.
05:00 Priya Rao: on benchmarking specifics: we'll run three scenarios — short prompt low latency, mixed workload (chat), and long generation (summarization). we'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE or custom eval).
05:30 Ethan Cole: for quality we'll supply 500 eval prompts with expected outputs and a scoring rubric.
05:38 Priya Rao: perfect. for cost comparatives we can run hosted first to get baseline unit costs then spin up Redwood Dedicated pool to test throughput and steady-state price. note: Dedicated gives predictable throughput but has different cost profile.
05:58 Sofia Nguyen: question around kv cache and batching — how does dedicated handle our long-context sessions?
06:06 Priya Rao: the runtime manages kv cache and we can tune continuous batching and prefix caching. small mismatch: sometimes the transcription system says KV cash but it's KV cache, ok.
06:20 Mark Anders: (joined) sorry for the delay, had a meeting. quick question: what's the rollback strategy if we hit perf regressions mid-POC?
06:34 Jordan Lee: we generally do model pinning and automated fallback to smaller variants or older model versions; plus we can throttle traffic to hosted tier while debugging.
06:46 Mark Anders: got it. also we may want to run a legal procurement check in parallel.
06:52 Ethan Cole: yes we'll loop procurement early.
07:00 Priya Rao: back to timeline and milestones: i'll share a detailed milestone doc after this call. milestones we propose:
07:10 - Kickoff (today)
07:14 - Access & infra setup (credentials, VPC peering, SSO)
07:20 - Baseline benchmarks (hosted)
07:25 - Dedicated throughput & stress tests
07:30 - Midpoint review (results, regressions, tunings)
07:36 - Stability run and final benchmarks
07:40 - Exec readout (business metrics, recommended config)
08:00 Sofia Nguyen: what about success criteria for quality — is the <3% regression on our eval set acceptable?
08:08 Ethan Cole: yes that's our ballpark.
08:12 Priya Rao: we'll include quality thresholds and failure definition in the benchmark spreadsheet.
08:22 Jordan Lee: quick note on dataset size — you said 50k records; is that representative?
08:29 Ethan Cole: yes 50k anonymized records covers our core edge cases, and we can include heavy long-form samples (~1k tokens) for stress.
08:40 Priya Rao: perfect. for ingestion we'll take a sampling approach: 10k initial seed for baseline then ramp to 50k for throughput/stability.
08:52 Luis Martinez: ops note: we will provide a runbook for S3 ingestion and credential rotation.
09:00 Aisha Khan: on keys — we insist on customer-managed keys for production, for POC managed keys are fine with NDA.
09:12 Jordan Lee: acknowledged. we'll add KMS notes.
09:20 Sofia Nguyen: do you have any benchmark artifacts or previous POC results we can look at?
09:27 Priya Rao: yes i'll attach example benchmark spreadsheets and a sample runbook. also a short benchmarks summary deck.
09:40 Ethan Cole: will Redwood run the baseline tests or do we expect Nebula to run them?
09:46 Priya Rao: Redwood will run the hosted baseline and we can support your team to run the dedicated tests. we'll also provide scripts to reproduce runs.
10:00 Ethan Cole: good. can we also capture cost metrics by token and by hour for the dedicated pool?
10:08 Jordan Lee: yes we'll include cost modeling scenarios.
10:12 Mark Anders: any limitations around model choices? can we bring a finetuned model?
10:18 Priya Rao: for dedicated we can serve customer finetuned models as long as format is compatible; for hosted there are some constraints but we can discuss. we'll need model artifacts and sizes to estimate mem requirements.
10:32 Sofia Nguyen: model size: our finetune is 13B, quantized to 4-bit, should fit on a 80GB A100 equivalent, but we need confirmation.
10:44 Priya Rao: we'll run sizing estimates after we get the model artefacts (note: transcription sometimes misses artefact vs artifact).
10:55 Jordan Lee: ok next up security checklist ownership — Aisha, are you comfortable with the timelines for security review?
11:03 Aisha Khan: yes timeline looks ok, plan to complete initial review by 2026-03-10. we'll prioritize SOC2 docs and SSO integration tests.
11:12 Luis Martinez: we'll share our SAML guide and audit log format.
11:20 Ethan Cole: can we get a short statement about data residency and retention policy for logs?
11:28 Jordan Lee: yes we'll include retention policy and log anonymization notes in the security pack.
11:36 Priya Rao: moving to success criteria recap: p95 latency < 500ms short prompts, cost < $0.03 per 1k tokens, quality regression < 3% on eval set, stability under 120 qps bursts for sustained 30s.
11:55 Sofia Nguyen: agreed.
12:00 Jordan Lee: recap of next steps: we'll share benchmark template and runbook, you provide dataset and credentials. set midpoint review 03-31, exec readout week of 04-20.
12:12 Ethan Cole: yep. any blockers on Redwood side?
12:18 Priya Rao: none. we'll need sample data and permissions.
12:24 Jordan Lee: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with docs and links.
12:30 Mark Anders: thanks.
12:32 Meeting end
